text:
ConocoPhillips fell 3.3% today as oil prices reversed earlier gains on growing hopes for a U.S.-Iran diplomatic deal. Reports that Iran could reopen the Strait of Hormuz within a week if U.S. military pressure eases have lifted expectations of a negotiated settlement to the U.S.-Iran conflict. Since oil prices had spiked on geopolitical tension, the prospect of de-escalation sent crude lower — U.S. oil dropped back below $100 per barrel on Monday and hasn't recovered. For an oil company like ConocoPhillips, lower crude prices directly reduce the profit margin on every barrel produced and refined.

The stock has also been sliding steadily for over a week, down 5% in two weeks as the broader oil market has shifted from pricing in Middle East supply disruptions toward pricing in potential supply normalization. The gap between U.S. crude ($107) and world oil prices ($131) suggests some regional supply uncertainty remains, but the diplomatic momentum is clearly weighing on near-term energy prices.
